name: queue_short_favourite_bid
status: pre-registered; no trade of this track has been simulated and no price or outcome of the L2 windows has been read; only touch-size coverage and the size percentiles below were looked at
question: Does a resting bid on the favourite side, joined only when the displayed queue ahead is short and filled only after that queue has printed, have a positive expectancy held to settlement?
owner_request: Pre-register one maker (resting-order) idea with an explicit queue-position model before touching data, then score it in-sample only. A null result is a success.
why_this_idea: Every maker result so far used sim_core's fill rule, which treats the order as first in line: it fills once 50 contracts print at or through the limit, whatever rests ahead of it. Touch sizes now exist, so that assumption can be replaced by first-in-first-out. A bid joined behind a deep queue fills only after a large sell flow, which is adverse; a bid joined behind a short queue fills on ordinary flow. The idea tests whether the short-queue favourite bid is worth resting once the queue is paid for. It is one rule, with no sweep.

queue_position_model.implemented_in: openkal/sim_core.py: Tape.queue_ahead, Tape.queue_fill and run_trade(queue_model=True); additive and off by default, the existing results unchanged
queue_position_model.queue_ahead: the contracts displayed at the order's price on the book row it arrives into: yes_bid_sz for a YES bid, yes_ask_sz for a NO bid (a NO bid's touch is the YES ask); a bid inside the spread has 0 ahead; a bid below the touch, a row with no size, or a tape with no sizes has an unknown queue and the order is skipped
queue_position_model.queue_moves_on: prints at the order's price from the aggressors that trade against it (YES sellers for a YES bid, YES buyers for a NO bid); nothing else moves it
queue_position_model.fill: first in, first out: filled when queue_ahead + own contracts have printed at the price, or at the first print strictly through the price; the order also needs the existing proof that at least 50 contracts printed at or through the price since it arrived; whole fills only
queue_position_model.conservative_simplifications: cancellations ahead of the order and size changes are not modelled, so the queue never shrinks except by prints and fills come later than they may in life
queue_position_model.arrival: 1 s after the decision, the canonical lag; prints at the arrival second do not count
queue_position_model.exit_legs: none in this idea; run_trade keeps the plain print-through rule for exit legs, so this does not touch them

data.tape: data/track10-tape (pinned, digests in pin.json), read only
data.l2_windows: settled window closes where every lane has finite touch sizes on more than half of its book rows: 46 windows, 2026-11-17 20:15 to 2026-11-18 11:00
data.touch_sizes_exist_from: 2026-11-17 20:06; before that the cache has no sizes and depth arrays are all NaN
data.no_other_data: no spot, index, flow or feature enters the rule

split.rule: chronological over the 46 L2 window closes: cut = l2_closes[int(0.6 * 46)] = l2_closes[27]
split.oos: closes at or after the cut are never loaded, simulated or counted by this track; they stay sealed (oos_scored null) and nothing here spends a look

rule.decision_points: for every lane and every IS window, at 660, 540, 420 and 300 seconds before the close, in that order
rule.one_position: once an order of a lane in a window fills, that lane-window takes no further order; an order that does not fill is cancelled after its patience and the next decision point may place another
rule.side: the favourite: the side with the higher best bid (YES bid against NO bid = 1 - yes ask); a tie is skipped
rule.queue_band: the queue ahead is known and at most 100 contracts, i.e. at most two full stakes; the 100 was read off the touch-size percentiles in known_before_registering, not off any outcome
rule.order: a post-only bid joined at the side's best bid, sized with sim_core.stake_qty at a stake of 65.58 USD (at most 50 contracts), patience 100 s, then cancelled
rule.exit: none: the position is held to settlement, no exit order, no fee beyond the zero maker entry fee
rule.all_orders_through: openkal/sim_core.py run_trade(entry_style=maker, queue_model=True); no price, fill or PnL is computed outside it

primary_statistic: mean net USD per filled trade in sample, the profit factor and the per-lane nets, from sim_core

is_bar.meaning: the same IS bar as the earlier tracks; clearing it earns a pre-registered OOS design, never an OOS look by itself
needs_all_of: one-sided window bootstrap p < 0.05 for mean net <= 0 (10000 draws, seed 0, resampling the IS window closes with replacement, the Track 10 procedure)
is_bar.no_multiplicity: one registered idea and one configuration, so no correction applies; the controls below are descriptive and decide nothing

controls_descriptive: the same orders under the old fill rule (queue_model False, 50 contracts at or through): how optimistic the old maker results were
the same rule with the queue longer than 100 contracts but known, under the queue model: whether long queues are the adverse ones
decision points by outcome: placed, filled, and each skip reason (no size, queue over 100, band, tie, no quote, crossed)
known_before_registering: touch sizes exist only from 2026-11-17 20:06; depth arrays are all NaN and gate_allow is constant 0, so only the touch queue is observable
the 46 L2 windows have sizes on more than half their rows in all four lanes; the 60/40 cut puts 27 windows in sample

displayed touch size percentiles 10/25/50/75/90 on valid rows: BTC 204/1175/4207/8723/13090, ETH 21/131/428/806/1248, SOL 6/53/181/506/707, XRP 5/45/250/408/687 contracts; so a 100-contract cap admits SOL, XRP and ETH often and BTC rarely

the earlier maker tracks all failed in sample or out of sample under the old fill rule: two-sided spread market making (Track 5), the Asian-settlement maker (Track 4B), passive_mm_fade (OOS 46 trades, -$57.50)
the market's ask is well calibrated in the band (Brier about 0.2376), so a favourite bought at its bid has an edge only of about the spread it saves, before adverse selection
Track 6's L2 tree models and Tracks 2C and 2D scored the same L2 windows with different rules; their OOS slices are sealed and unread
expected: fewer than 30 fills in sample, so the bar is not cleared and the result is a null. Most decision points will skip on the queue cap or the band. If the primary does fill 30 or more and loses, the queue model has done its job; if it clears the bar, the next step is a pre-registered OOS design, not a look.
